newsitem.title: UK: European gas oil prices ease, but demand strong.
newsitem.headline: European gas oil prices ease, but demand strong.

text.p: European gas oil prices eased around $4.00 with futures on Friday, but demand for diesel and German heating oil remained very strong, traders said.
October IPE shed $3.25 to $228.75 per tonne, but dealers said this was a brief correction in the bull market.
"Both grades, heating oil and diesel, will continue to strengthen, and we could see heating oil premiums in double figures when October expires," a U.K. refiner said.
He saw limited bearish pressure from the 400,000 tonnes of U.S. material entering Europe, partly because demand was so strong and partly because only 100,000 tonnes of it conformed to

One of the latter cargoes was sold on Friday at Oct IPE +$15.50 cif NWE, although smaller cargoes were valued $3 higher. Diesel premiums to November futures were slightly stronger on Friday, talked at $18-22 for second half delivery.

However, some dealers saw weakness in the heating oil and Russian markets, possible related to aggressive selling of a poor quality U.S. cargo. A U.S. trader was heard offering 53,000 tonnes for Oct 10 arrival down to Oct +$2.50, bid at +$1.00.
Russian premiums were suffering too, with two or three prompt cargoes talked as low as $5.00 cif.
